definitions.explanation: A person who accompanies someone, especially as a servant or escort.

examples.japanese: {殿様|とのさま}は{供|とも}を{連|つ}れて{旅|たび}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: The lord set out on a journey with his attendants.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}を{供|とも}に{連|つ}れて{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went shopping with my child accompanying me.

examples.japanese: {供|とも}をする{者|もの}は{三人|さんにん}だった。
examples.english: There were three people in the retinue.

notes:
{供|とも} refers to someone who accompanies another person, often in a subordinate role. It has a somewhat classical or formal feel.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {供|とも}を{連|つ}れる: to bring attendants/companions
- {供|とも}をする: to accompany someone (as an attendant)
- お{供|とも}する: to accompany (humble form)

NOTE: This word appears in {子供|こども} (child), though the connection is historical. The character {供|とも/ども} can also be a pluralizing suffix (e.g., {私|わたし}{供|ども} = we, humble).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {連れ|つれ}: companion (more casual)
- {随行|ずいこう}: accompanying (formal, for officials)
